objective: Coordinator's go-ahead (18 November 2026) after TREE-STEPS-20261118-001's referee: on a mixed cycle (a not-all-equal path closed by a parity knot) the irreducible-set distance misreads the parity knot; find a distance that reads freedom (the knot test's K2) rather than zero correlation, agreeing with bond distance there while keeping the tree results, or prove none exists. Answer found before the freeze: bond distance itself (sets on which the states form a knot, K1-K3) is steps apart plus one on every knot tree under any mixture of parity and not-all-equal knots (a short proof) and reads the cycle's parity knot as one knot. This study proves it, checks it one size past, and compares freedom (bond distance) with correlation (tau, delta, delta_K) where they part: on cycles. Serves G1 and G16; tests A97; B200.
status: Complete 2026-11-18 (Successful; referee pending): the distance that reads freedom is bond distance, the knot test applied to sets: steps apart plus one on every knot tree of parity, not-all-equal and betweenness knots in any mixture (proved), hub-free, reading the mixed cycle's parity knot as one knot; computed on 103,248 tree pairs, rings and mixed cycles (7 of 7 held).
